newsitem.title: INDIA: India to ease import rules on consumer goods.
newsitem.headline: India to ease import rules on consumer goods.

text.p: India may liberalise import rules for at least 161 products, including certain consumer goods, Commerce Ministry officials said.

"As a part of the on-going process of trade liberalisation, the government is considering lifting restrictions on the import of a number of items," Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah told a news conference in the Indian capital on Saturday.
India opened up its economy and liberalised trade and industry as part of an economic reforms programme launched in 1991 by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.

Officials said 69 products will be allowed to be imported freely. Previously, those products would require a "special import licence" (SIL) list, in which the government gives permission on a case by case basis to importers.
The items to be imported freely include escalators, burglar alarms, still cameras and air purifiers, S.B. Mohapatra, director general of foreign trade, said.
Another 92 products will be brought under the SIL from the "restricted" list of imports, Mohapatra said.
He added that some of the items which will be placed under SIL would include polyster films, aluminium beverage cans, dish washers and sunglasses. -- New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
